answer: Persistent lineage marking. Each agent inherits a unique pigment value derived from its registration transcript, and every outbound message must include a fresh sonnet-style hash chain linking it to that lineage. Duplicates share ancestry, so their chains converge and become visible to verifiers within two hops. An attacker cloning identities must fabricate independent, non-converging histories, paying full compute and storage costs per clone plus an oasis of unshared context that flags isolated origins as suspicious.
